title: Longest Balanced Bit Run
statement: You get an array bits that contains only 0 and 1. Find the longest contiguous run that has as many 0s as 1s, and return its length. Return 0 if there is no such run.

examples.why: The first four bits [0, 1, 1, 0] have two of each. No longer run is balanced: the whole array has six 1s.
No run contains a 0, so none can be balanced.
The whole array has three of each. The 0s and 1s do not need to alternate.

hints: Turn every 0 into −1. What does a balanced run look like now?
A balanced run sums to 0. With prefix sums, the run from i + 1 to j sums to 0 exactly when prefix[i] equals prefix[j].

Store the first index where each prefix value appears, starting with value 0 at index −1. At every j, if the current prefix was seen before at index i, the run i + 1..j is balanced; its length is j − i.

explain.intuition:
Counting "as many 0s as 1s" gets easy if you score every 1 as +1 and every 0 as −1. Then a run is balanced exactly when its score is 0. Now keep a running score from the start of the array. The score of a run from i + 1 to j is score[j] − score[i], so the run is balanced exactly when the running score has the same value at i and at j.

So the question becomes: for each position, where did I first see this running score? The farther back, the longer the run. A map from score to first index answers that in O(1). Seed it with score 0 at index −1, so runs that start at the very beginning are counted too.
steps: Create a map first with first[0] = −1, and set score = 0, best = 0.
For each index j, add +1 for a 1 and −1 for a 0 to score.
If score is in first, update best = max(best, j − first[score]).
Otherwise store first[score] = j. Never overwrite an existing entry: the earliest index gives the longest run.
pitfalls: Forgetting the seed first[0] = −1. Then a run that starts at index 0, like the whole array in the third example, is missed.
Updating the stored index every time a score repeats. Later indexes give shorter runs.
Using a sliding window. Adding an element can unbalance the run and a later one rebalance it, so there is no rule for when to shrink.

solutions.title: Check every start
solutions.idea: For each start index, extend the run to the right while keeping a +1/−1 score, and record the length whenever the score is 0.

solutions.title: Running score with first-seen map
solutions.idea: Score 1 as +1 and 0 as −1. Two positions with the same running score bound a balanced run, so remember where each score first appeared.

followups: The scores only range from −n to n. How can you replace the map with an array?
Count how many balanced runs there are instead of finding the longest.
